decisions.reason: As an automation product already backed in 2024 and closely aligned with the firm's digital-control strategy, management is likely to stay committed because prior engineering investment and public positioning make any still-limited uptake look temporary rather than decisive.

Although this flap weir is less central to the firm's digital future than software-heavy offers, it remains close to the core water-infrastructure business, so management would usually give a recently launched hardware product more time before reversing course.

The energy management system fits especially well with the firm's stated move toward networked, efficient and energy-recovering infrastructure, so sunk development effort and strong strategic visibility make withdrawal unlikely within a year.

Because this overflow flap gate was introduced as a multi-model product line with its own dedicated presentation, management has made a visible commitment and is likely to continue supporting it unless results become clearly untenable.
